chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hafs al-Kalbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'Indeed, God (Mighty and Majestic) sent His Messenger with Islam to the people for ten years, but they refused to accept until He commanded him to fight. Thus, the good is in the sword and beneath the sword, and the matter will return just as it began.'

key_terms.السَّيْفِ: The sword, metaphor for legitimate armed struggle in Islam
key_terms.بِالْقِتَالِ: With fighting/warfare; here jihad in defense and for spreading justice
key_terms.رَسُولَهُ: His Messenger, referring to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a common divine epithet
key_terms.يَعُودُ كَمَا بَدَأَ: The matter will return as it began — interpreted as a prophetic statement about the return of the Imam

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'the good is in the sword' mean in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) recounts that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) spent ten years peacefully inviting people to Islam before divine permission was granted for armed struggle. The declaration 'the good is in the sword and beneath the sword' addresses the early Muslim community's question about the legitimacy of jihad, affirming that after exhausting peaceful means, forceful defense became obligatory. The final statement — 'the matter will return as it began' — is interpreted by Shia scholars as a reference to the occultation of the Imam and the necessity of a future rising (qiyam) to restore the rule of justice.
